title: Continue
summary: An open-source coding agent with IDE and CLI distribution; current sources give conflicting lifecycle signals by channel.

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: AI coding assistant for VS Code and JetBrains, with Agent, Chat, Edit, autocomplete and CLI surfaces documented.

facts.label: Agent permissions
facts.value: Agent mode can use tools to modify a codebase; the docs describe per-tool permission prompts by default.

facts.label: Self-hosted model endpoint
facts.value: Continue documents connecting to self-hosted model endpoints and provides an offline IDE setup that installs a VS Code extension, disables anonymous telemetry and configures a local model. This documented path does not establish offline behavior for every client or account route, and no installation was tested.

facts.label: Local model inference
facts.value: Continue lists local models served through Ollama and warns that sufficient VRAM is needed and limited tool-calling/reasoning can make Agent mode challenging. Its offline guide also requires disabling anonymous telemetry and configuring a local model; model quality and actual data flow were not tested.

facts.label: Ownership and code availability
facts.value: Continue's official site says it was acquired by Cursor and that its open-source codebase remains freely available as a foundation. This does not establish maintenance or support commitments for each distribution channel.

facts.label: CLI workflow and access
facts.value: Continue documents `cn` as a terminal coding agent that can edit files, run commands and handle multi-step tasks; it describes the same agent as its IDE extensions. The CLI quickstart lists a Continue account or Anthropic API key, and Node.js 20+ for the npm installation path. It does not establish account or provider prices or data terms.

facts.label: Distribution lifecycle statements
facts.value: The repository README says continuedev/continue is read-only and no longer actively maintained, and describes a final 2.0.0 release for the VS Code extension, CLI and JetBrains plugin. The JetBrains Marketplace calls its plugin community-maintained and recommends the CLI, saying active development is happening there. The CLI statements conflict; the sources do not establish the current supported package, security response or a support commitment.

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: Continue's Privacy Notice was last updated 2026-02-05. It describes log data (including IP, device, OS/browser, URLs/referrers, usage time and errors) and analytics/activity data from open-source offerings unless users opt out of data sharing. It says the notice does not cover Customer Content processed on a customer's behalf when Continue acts as a processor. The notice's post-acquisition applicability, client settings, actual traffic and selected model-provider handling were not verified.

facts.label: MCP support
facts.value: Continue docs describe configurable MCP servers as tools for Agent mode; upstream distribution and maintenance remain separate open questions.

prices.name: Model and account usage
prices.billing: Confirm the current Continue account or model-provider route and its usage terms.

sections.heading: Separate acquisition, source availability and support
paragraphs: Continue's official site says it was acquired by Cursor and that its open-source codebase remains freely available as a foundation. Code availability does not establish who supports each package or how security issues are handled.

sections.heading: Resolve the channel-specific lifecycle conflict
paragraphs: The upstream README calls the repository read-only and describes a final 2.0.0 release across the VS Code extension, CLI and JetBrains plugin. The JetBrains Marketplace calls its plugin community-maintained and recommends the CLI, saying active development is happening there. These CLI statements conflict. Confirm the exact distribution, publisher, version, update channel and security response before depending on it.

sections.heading: Check CLI access and model terms
paragraphs: The CLI quickstart describes `cn` as the terminal coding agent behind the IDE extensions and lists a Continue account or Anthropic API key; its npm installation path requires Node.js 20+. Confirm the applicable billing and data terms for the chosen account or provider separately.

sections.heading: Treat offline support as a configured path
paragraphs: Continue documents an offline IDE setup that installs a VS Code extension, disables anonymous telemetry and configures a local model. This is a documented setup path, not a test of a specific version or every client and account mode.

sections.heading: Read privacy coverage by role and date
paragraphs: The published Privacy Notice is dated 2026-02-05. It describes open-source product log and analytics categories unless users opt out, and explicitly excludes customer content processed on a customer's behalf when Continue acts as a processor. Confirm that this notice applies to the selected post-acquisition product and review model-provider terms separately.

pros.text: Continue documents `cn` as a terminal coding agent that can edit files, run commands and work through multi-step tasks.
Continue documents configurable MCP servers as custom tools for Agent mode.

cons.text: Continue's documentation says MCP can only be used in Agent mode.

Continue's README says the repository is read-only and calls 2.0.0 its final release, while the JetBrains Marketplace calls that plugin community-maintained and says active development is happening in the CLI; confirm the exact channel's support path.

faqs.question: Can Continue use MCP outside Agent mode?
faqs.answer: No. Continue's MCP documentation says MCP can only be used in Agent mode.

faqs.question: What do Continue's current sources say about package maintenance?
faqs.answer: The README says the repository is read-only and describes a final 2.0.0 release, while JetBrains Marketplace calls its plugin community-maintained and recommends the CLI as the active development path. Those CLI statements conflict, so they do not establish a current supported package or support commitment.

faqs.question: What does the Continue CLI quickstart require?
faqs.answer: It describes `cn` as a terminal coding agent and lists a Continue account or Anthropic API key; Node.js 20+ is required for the npm installation path. The quickstart does not establish the applicable price or provider data terms.

faqs.question: Can Continue be configured to run offline with a local model?
faqs.answer: Continue documents a VS Code setup that installs the extension, turns off Allow Anonymous Telemetry and configures a local model. This is a documented path, not verification of a particular build or every Continue client and account mode.

verdict: Treat Continue as a conditional candidate. Official sources confirm the acquisition and code availability but conflict about CLI lifecycle; verify the exact package, updates and security response, and do not infer a support commitment from published docs or marketplace availability.
bestFor: Developers evaluating configurable IDE coding assistance with an explicit maintenance check
notFor: Teams requiring a confirmed actively maintained upstream before evaluation
migration: Pin the exact extension or CLI version, export its configuration and model endpoints, and retain a tested fallback before rollout.
gaps: Resolve the README's final-release/read-only statements against the JetBrains Marketplace's CLI active-development statement; confirm the package, publisher, current version/update path and security response before publication or adoption.

Confirm the post-acquisition privacy notice's applicability, selected client/CLI telemetry settings and data flow, customer-content processing when Continue acts as a processor, and the selected model provider's data terms; no client, account or network traffic was inspected.
Confirm Continue account/model-provider billing; the CLI quickstart lists access methods but not their prices.
